speaker: expecting_mother
quote: my OB wrote a note for me requesting an accommodation for me to be fully remote effective 32 weeks. Well, since then my boss has come up with these dire tasks that I HAVE to be in office for.
context: First-time mother at 36+4 in an HR role with a long commute.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: she told me that I've been "consistently dropping the ball" because of all of the personal stuff I have going on at home (pregnancy, I just recently moved into a new home that had to get a deep clean because they found mold, my commute to my OB etc.)
context: Her boss's feedback weeks before her leave.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: As a result, she said that when I return from leave, I now have to come in every day until I can "prove myself"... At WHAT? Printing things in color?
context: Boss reversed an agreed hybrid schedule for after her leave.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I personally don't want to put my son in daycare if I don't have to. 1 - because of cost and 2 - I'm neurotic and have seen too many horror stories.
context: Why she asked for a part-remote schedule after leave.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Or should I wait it out until after my maternity leave? I'm just concerned about not having a new job lined up by the time leave is over..
context: Applying for remote roles before her due date.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: Today, my ob approved my maternity leave effective immediately. I feel like a failure because I really didn’t want to take time away from my baby, and wanted to work until she came. But I just physically could not do it.
context: 37 weeks, weeks of strong contractions; first pregnancy was ten years ago.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: It was embarrassing and making people extremely uncomfortable when I would have a contraction in the office.
context: Why she stopped working at 37 weeks.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: My first pregnancy was a breeze, but it was also 10 years ago. So that’s all I have to compare this pregnancy to.
context: Second pregnancy after a ten-year gap.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: AND I have to go into work every day and pretend like everything is ok like all the women before me???
context: Nearly third trimester, symptoms getting worse each week.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I can’t sleep a full night with all the tossing and turning and peeing, and I’m getting so big not just from being pregnant, but also not being able to workout, which used to be my happy place.
context: Post titled 'I hate being pregnant'.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: The 2nd trimester boost did not happen to me and it has just been a rocky ride from the beginning - there was never a moment when things let up for me.
context: First-time mother at 35 weeks.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Anytime anyone would ask me how I’m doing or how pregnancy was, I would not sugarcoat it by any means and would tell them how terrible it’s been. Even though my symptoms have been miserable, me and my baby are completely healthy and so I’m just feeling this weight of guilt all of a sudden.
context: Near her due date, guilty for complaining.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: On one hand, I think we should all try more honest about our experiences, but I also don’t want to scare anyone who might be trying or wanting to try soon.
context: Weighing honesty about a hard pregnancy.

speaker: parent_unspecified
quote: People told me my energy would come back during the second trimester and while I feel like it may have gotten a little bit better, my third trimester is back to the same thing.
context: 32 weeks, works in healthcare on her feet.

speaker: parent_unspecified
quote: I try to walk during my lunch breaks, but that’s been difficult recently too due to the heat and general exhaustion. I also wake up at 4-5 am Mon-Fri for work
context: Plans to keep working until her due date.

speaker: parent_unspecified
quote: I really wanted to stay fit and active and continue to lift weights and eat healthy during this pregnancy as I did before, but I come home and immediately crash. Fast food and takeout have become a weakness that I cannot say no to
context: 32 weeks, usually very active.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I started driving to the grocery store and I got so tired I just turned around and came back. My toddler was so confused. lol
context: 10.5 weeks; forgot how tiring the first trimester was.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: She quite literally told me during my 13wk appointment “you should be feeling great now!”
context: 23+5, still exhausted and sleeping badly.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I was told I was supposed to be feeling great and energized in the second trimester?? But I have yet to experience that (23+5).
context: Opening of a post on second-trimester exhaustion.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I’ve tried milk/cottage cheese before bed (as suggested by OB), and even eating pineapple at dinner (it’s supposed to help release melatonin).
context: Sleep tricks tried at 23 weeks.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Im struggling to pay for this pregnancy as it is and I already have a follow up ultrasound next week, so I didnt call the Dr's office again.
context: Just under 14 weeks; cost kept her from calling about a symptom.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: At the beginning of my third trimester, we bought a new bigger car to accommodate three kiddos. Of course since then, I’ve read that new car smells are toxic, full of VOCs, etc.
context: Expecting her third child; same post also in r/BabyBumps.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: But the VOCs and brain development Google was a guilties doom spiral.
context: Reply in her own thread.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Got ready for work, was feeling good about my outfit and the nausea came.
context: End of the first trimester, vomiting before work.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Lawd this child better be cute because pregnancy sure as hell is not cute.
context: After vomiting hard enough to wet herself.

speaker: parent_unspecified
quote: my state has a new parental leave program where the birthing parent is eligible for up to 12 weeks of medical leave, then can claim 8 weeks of bonding leave so 20 total.
context: Her understanding of her state's new leave program.

speaker: parent_unspecified
quote: I turned in the paperwork that my work required my doc fill out to the state program. They noted the doc only said I need 6 - 8 weeks, instead of 12 weeks.
context: Leave paperwork came back short of the maximum.

speaker: parent_unspecified
quote: I’m curious those of you who got your OB to fill out the paperwork indicating you needed 12 weeks, how did you go about that?
context: Asking others how they got a longer medical-leave certification.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I made it clear to my husband I don’t want visitors postpartum for at least 3 weeks. People can come meet baby in the hospital in a controlled environment but I don’t want to host people after that.
context: Due tomorrow with her first daughter.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I have a big worry that his mom will just show up at our house post partum and then since she’s already here, guilt her way into coming inside.
context: Her husband has not yet told his mother the visitor rule.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: At this point he got irritated with me and just told me to stop talking about it because he’s gonna deal with it and he’s going to tell her when he’s going to tell her. He said I’m too “pushy” when it comes to his family
context: Asking her husband to tell his mother before the hospital.
